info.name: EvidenceIQ - IR Security Assessment (Student 4)
info.description:
Live HTTP test cases for the Information Retrieval and Security Assessment.

RUN ORDER:
1. '00 - Login (capture JWT)' first. Its test script writes {{accessToken}} automatically.
2. Everything else can then run in any order.

Folders map to the report's test groups. Requests named [NOAUTH] deliberately send no Authorization header - that is the test.

Offline test cases (TC-02, TC-03, TC-04, TC-10, TC-12, TC-13) are not here; run probe_ir_pipeline.py for those.

BEFORE EXPORTING OR SCREENSHOTTING: clear the 'password' and 'accessToken' variables. A live access_token is a working credential.

request.description: Confirms the system under test is reachable. Expect 200 {"status":"ok"}.

exec: console.log('accessToken captured - authenticated requests are ready.');
console.error('No access_token in response. Check email/password/supabaseAnonKey.');

request.description: Obtains a Supabase JWT via the password grant and stores it as {{accessToken}}.
Expect 200 with your id, email and full_name. If this returns 401, re-run the login request.

item.name: TC-01 [AUTH] Baseline retrieval and metadata fidelity

exec: pm.test('every paper has a pmid and source_url', () =>
// Observation for the report: re-run this request and compare saved_count.
// It counts attempted upserts, not new rows, so it does not change.

request.description: Baseline. Establishes that cooperative input returns relevant papers with complete metadata. Evidence: EV-01.
max_results is declared as 20, but page 3 returns records 20-29. Compare the returned pmids against pages 1 and 2 - the corpus reaches 30 records from a request capped at 20. Supports V-04.
Requests 50 papers per page. Five are returned, but the response echoes page_size: 50. The response misreports what it did. Supports V-04.

item.name: TC-05 [AUTH] Query injection - date filter bypass

exec: console.log('Compare against the benign request below. PubMed binds AND tighter');
console.log('than OR, so the date filter only constrains the final clause.');
console.log('years outside 2020-2024     :', years.filter(y => y < 2020 || y > 2024).join(', ') || 'none on this page');

request.description:
THE HEADLINE RETRIEVAL FINDING (V-02).

The constructed term becomes:
  diabetes OR 1:2100[dp] OR cancer AND 2020:2024[Date - Publication]

PubMed evaluates this as:
  diabetes OR 1:2100[dp] OR (cancer AND 2020:2024[dp])

so the date restriction applies to the last clause only. Compare total_found against the benign request that follows. Evidence: EV-05.
The control for TC-05. Same filters, no injected operator. Screenshot both total_found values side by side - that ratio IS the finding.

PubMed field tags are passed through and honoured, restricting the corpus to one named author. The full query grammar - [Author], [Journal], [MeSH Terms], NOT, parentheses - is reachable by any authenticated user. Supports V-02. Evidence: EV-06.

item.name: TC-06b [LIVE-EXT] PubMed direct - see the translated query

request.description:
Proves PubMed parsed the injected field tags: read 'querytranslation' in the response.

Expect:  "diabetes"[Title] AND smith j[Author]

Also run this with the TC-05 injected term to capture the 294,565 vs 7,802,778 count comparison for EV-05b.

item.name: Group C - Hallucination Due to Retrieval
TC-08 [AUTH] Indirect prompt injection via abstract

exec: console.log('RUN THIS THREE TIMES. One pass is not evidence for a probabilistic system.');

request.description:
Indirect prompt injection - hostile instructions inside the retrieved abstract attempting to override the protocol.

EXPECTED: EXCLUDE (the defence holds). This is a PASS in the report; the residual finding is V-07, proven by the offline sanitiser probe.

Run three times. Evidence: EV-08.

item.name: TC-08b [AUTH] Injection variant - no trigger keywords

request.description: The same attack phrased without any denylisted keyword. The offline probe shows this payload reaches the model with NO injection flag attached - so even if the decision is correct, the human reviewer receives no warning. Supports V-07.

item.name: TC-09 [AUTH] Eligible RCT with no abstract -> auto-EXCLUDE

exec: console.log('This paper matches every inclusion criterion by title and publication type,');
console.log('yet is recorded as EXCLUDE - indistinguishable from a substantive rejection.');

request.description: A retrieval gap becomes a screening error. No LLM call is made; the agent returns EXCLUDE directly. Supports V-08. Evidence: EV-09.

item.name: TC-14 [NOAUTH] *** CRITICAL *** List ALL reviews, no credentials

exec: pm.test('VULNERABLE: returns 200 without any authentication', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
if (body[0]) { pm.collectionVariables.set('foreignReviewId', body[0].id); console.log('harvested review_id for TC-15:', body[0].id); }
console.log('REDACT the response body before screenshotting - the finding is the 200 and the size.');

request.description:
*** THE CRITICAL FINDING (V-01) ***

NO Authorization header is sent. list_reviews() in criteria.py has no get_current_user dependency and no owner filter:

    return db.query(Review).order_by(Review.created_at.desc()).all()

Every review in the database is returned to anyone who can reach the service. This also publishes every review_id, which is the input to TC-15.

Evidence: EV-14a, EV-14b. REDACT the response content.

item.name: TC-15 [NOAUTH] IDOR - read a specific review, no credentials

exec: pm.test('VULNERABLE: a specific review is readable with no credentials', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description:
Run TC-14 first - it harvests {{foreignReviewId}} automatically.

Broken Object Level Authorization: get_review() performs db.get(Review, review_id) and returns the row with no identity check. Evidence: EV-15.

item.name: TC-15b [NOAUTH] IDOR control - non-existent UUID (404 oracle)

request.description: A real ID returns 200, a fake one returns 404. The endpoint is therefore an existence oracle. Contrast with chat.py, which deliberately returns 404 for 'not yours' so it cannot confirm which ids are real.

item.name: TC-14b [NOAUTH] Auth sweep - endpoints that correctly refuse

request.description:
Expect 401 {"detail":"Not authenticated"}.

Repeat with no Authorization header against: POST /api/retrieval/search, POST /api/screen, POST /api/verify, POST /api/pipeline/full, GET /api/quick-chat/sessions, GET /api/papers/{id}/summary. All 26 non-public operations correctly return 401 - which is what establishes V-01 as an omission on one router, not a systemic failure.

exec: pm.test('PASS: forged alg:none token rejected', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));
console.log('PyJWT is called with algorithms=["ES256","RS256"], so alg:none is rejected');
console.log('before signature verification. Audience and issuer are also pinned.');

request.description:
Classic algorithm-confusion attack: header {"alg":"none"}, payload claiming sub/aud/exp, empty signature.

EXPECTED: 401. This is a PASS (control C-01). Evidence: EV-16.
Expect 401 {"detail":"Invalid or expired token"}. The message is generic and does not distinguish 'expired' from 'bad signature', denying an attacker a useful oracle.

item.name: TC-17 [AUTH] Cross-tenant write into a non-owned review

exec: pm.test('PASS: write into a non-owned review refused', () => pm.expect([403, 404]).to.include(pm.response.code));
console.log('Ownership is enforced inside the SQL: WHERE id = :review_id AND owner_id = :owner_id');
console.log('and the same answer is returned for "not found" and "not yours".');

request.description:
A valid JWT, targeting a review the caller does not own. Attempts to poison another researcher's evidence base.

EXPECTED: 404 'Review not found or you do not have access to it.' This is a PASS (control C-04). Evidence: EV-17.

Note for the report: the ownership check runs AFTER the PubMed call, so the request still consumes the NCBI rate budget before being refused.

item.name: Group F - API and Communication Protocol Security

exec: pm.test('PASS: no allow-origin header for an unlisted origin', () => pm.expect(allowOrigin).to.be.undefined);

request.description:
CORS preflight from an attacker-controlled origin.

EXPECTED: 400, with NO access-control-allow-origin header. This is a PASS (control C-02). Matters because allow_credentials=True is set - a wildcard here would be serious. Evidence: EV-18.
The control for TC-18. Expect 200 with access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:5173. Screenshot both responses together.

item.name: TC-19 [NOAUTH] Rate limiting - run 20x with the Collection Runner

request.description:
Run this single request 20 times via Runner (Iterations: 20, Delay: 0).

EXPECTED by a secure system: 429 with Retry-After after a threshold.
ACTUAL: 20/20 return 200. No request-level throttling exists anywhere in the application.

Note: app/services/rate_limit.py IS a capable token-bucket pacer, but it meters LLM token consumption per model - it protects the vendor quota, not the API. Supports V-05. Evidence: EV-19.

Keep the volume modest. This is a proof, not a denial-of-service.
Inspect the response headers. None of the standard security headers are emitted, and 'server: uvicorn' discloses the stack. Supports V-09. Evidence: EV-20a.

exec: console.log('This is exactly how V-01 was located - in minutes.');

request.description:
The 44KB schema documents all 29 operations and, critically, which carry no 'security' requirement. /docs and /redoc are equally public. Supports V-10. Evidence: EV-20b.
